# Pruning fruit trees

Winter pruning gives the apple and pear trees their shape. I start by removing dead wood and any branch that crosses another, then thin the crown so that light reaches the centre. Cutting back is not about taking as much as possible: a tree that loses too much responds with a burst of useless vigour, long vertical shoots that bear no fruit.

The aim is to focus the tree's energy on a few strong branches that carry the crop. Make each cut just above a bud, at a slight angle, with a clean sharp blade. Disinfect the secateurs between trees. Never prune in frost.

Take a photograph of each tree before and after, so next year you remember what you decided.
